design_decisions.decision: A periodic esp_timer callback polling hal_button_is_pressed(), not a dedicated FreeRTOS task.
design_decisions.why: The first real-hardware attempt used a dedicated xTaskCreate task (3072-byte stack) and caused a real, on-device-only heap exhaustion regression (see real_defects_found_this_sub_slice). esp_timer callbacks dispatch from the system's own shared esp_timer task, so the poller now costs zero new task stack -- only a few bytes of function-local state.

design_decisions.decision: Debounce: 50ms poll period, 3 consecutive 'pressed' reads (~150ms sustained) before treating a press as one trusted event; an 'armed' flag requires a full release-then-press cycle before re-arming.
design_decisions.why: Real mechanical button bounce is on the order of a few ms to a few tens of ms; ~150ms of sustained level is comfortably past that without making a real press feel unresponsive. Holding the button down must not repeatedly fire new grants from one physical press.

design_decisions.decision: physical_presence_grant_create_from_button() creates an 'ambient' grant matching ANY action class and ANY session, rather than trying to guess which of plan #20's 9 action classes or which caller session a single button press was 'for'.
design_decisions.why: One GPIO edge carries no information about installer intent. An ambient, WPS-style 'press then act within the window' grant is the only honest model for a single undifferentiated button; it still respects the same 60-second lifetime and one-time consume() semantics as an explicitly-bound grant, and a second create()/create_from_button() call always fully replaces (never merges with) whatever grant existed before.

design_decisions.decision: provisioning_secret_provider_get() is called exactly once, in WebServer::start(), and cached in a new provisioning_secret_ member -- not re-fetched per request.
design_decisions.why: The development adapter generates fresh random bytes on every call; fetching once and caching is what makes a real challenge/response flow possible at all (installer reads the value the boot log printed once, submits it back later). A fetch failure leaves the member default-constructed/empty, so provisioning_secret_matches() can never succeed against it -- fails closed, not open.

design_decisions.decision: config.max_uri_handlers raised from 24 to 56, not to some other value.
design_decisions.why: The real production route count is 44 (24 legacy + 20 v1, counted directly from register_web_routes()/register_web_routes_v1()) -- 56 gives 12 slots of real headroom for near-future routes (certificate rotation, #12) without needing another HIL round to catch the same class of bug again.

design_decisions.decision: Button poll timer creation failure is logged but not fatal to WebServer::start().
design_decisions.why: Every physical-presence-gated route already fails closed on its own when no grant exists (403 kPhysicalPresenceRequired). A missing button poller degrades to 'that one feature never works' rather than taking down the entire production listener over a secondary mechanism.

real_defects_found_this_sub_slice.defect: httpd_register_uri_handler: no slots left for registering handler -- production listener failed to start on real hardware.
real_defects_found_this_sub_slice.root_cause: config.max_uri_handlers was 24, a value set long before this session's work; the real production route total (legacy register_web_routes() 24 + v1 register_web_routes_v1() 20, this sub-slice's own new auth routes among them) is 44. Neither the host httpd mock (always accepts a registration unconditionally) nor compile/link verification can catch a runtime resource-limit exhaustion like this.
real_defects_found_this_sub_slice.how_found: Real idf.py encrypted-flash to the connected ESP32-C6, real serial boot capture -- not simulated or guessed.
real_defects_found_this_sub_slice.fix: config.max_uri_handlers raised to 56 (12-slot real headroom over the current 44-route total).

real_defects_found_this_sub_slice.defect: Deferred Zigbee start task creation failed -- heap exhaustion right before the pre-existing deferred-Zigbee-start xTaskCreate call.
real_defects_found_this_sub_slice.root_cause: A new dedicated FreeRTOS task for button polling (3072-byte stack) was added on top of an already-marginal post-boot heap budget (MQTT client init alone consumes roughly 17KB, confirmed via a real heap_caps_get_largest_free_block(MALLOC_CAP_8BIT)/heap_caps_get_free_size(MALLOC_CAP_INTERNAL) reading taken on real hardware, pre-existing and unrelated to this session's changes). Free heap right before the Zigbee task's own xTaskCreate call dropped to ~4500 bytes total / 2240 bytes largest contiguous block, below the 4096 bytes the Zigbee task's own stack needed.
real_defects_found_this_sub_slice.how_found: Temporary ESP_LOGW heap diagnostics added to web_server.cpp and main/app_main.cpp on real hardware, comparing against an earlier same-session HIL round where the identical Zigbee task creation succeeded before this sub-slice's button-task code existed. Diagnostics removed via targeted Edit once the fix was confirmed (never via git checkout, to avoid discarding other real uncommitted work in the same files).
real_defects_found_this_sub_slice.fix: Replaced the dedicated xTaskCreate button-poll task with a periodic esp_timer callback (dispatches from the shared system esp_timer task, costing zero new task stack). Verified fix: free heap right before Zigbee task creation went from a failing 4500/2240 bytes (total/largest) to a passing 7856/7680 bytes, and the deferred Zigbee task now creates successfully again.

PASS. User physically pressed and released the real BOOT button (GPIO9) on the connected board. Real serial capture shows exactly one log line, no bounce/double-fire: `I (1362795) web_server: Physical presence grant created from a trusted button press`, appearing ~23 seconds into the capture window, with no panics or errors around it. This confirms the full chain end to end: GPIO9 electrical level -> hal_button_is_pressed() -> esp_timer debounce callback -> physical_presence_grant_create_from_button() -> log line, on real hardware, from a real physical action, not simulated.

honest_scope_boundary: No physical-presence-gated route (auth/password, provisioning/enroll, factory-reset/operations) was exercised end-to-end over a real HTTPS request against the real device this round -- only the grant-creation half of the chain (button -> grant) was verified on hardware. The route-side consumption of a button-created grant is covered by host tests (mocked hal_button) but not by a real HTTPS client request against the flashed device.

Certificate rotation (plan #12) remains fully deferred -- recon only, no code written, scope explicitly flagged as comparable in size to this whole sub-slice and not meaningfully host-testable (new client-side mbedtls TLS code, a new persisted activation/rollback state machine, a temporary second local httpd_ssl listener).

The debounce constants (50ms poll, 3 consecutive reads) were chosen from general mechanical-switch bounce characteristics, not measured against this specific button/board's actual bounce profile with an oscilloscope or logic analyzer -- the real HIL press test confirms the chosen values work in practice (single clean event, no double-fire) but does not establish safety margin against a worse-bouncing unit.
releaseability: The physical-presence grant creation path (button -> grant) is now real, wired, and confirmed on real hardware end-to-end including a genuine physical button press. Two real, hardware-only-discoverable defects (URI handler slot exhaustion; heap exhaustion from the button task's own stack) were found and fixed on real hardware, not guessed or assumed. Route-side consumption of the grant is host-test-covered but not yet HIL-exercised over a real HTTPS request. No live production deployment yet (see memory project-not-yet-in-production.md).
